company_name: Dr. Ing. h.c. F. Porsche AG

equity_bridge.note: FS operating profit EUR 259m FY2025 (278m FY2024), RoS 5.9%; ~EUR 180m after 30% tax, capitalised at ~8x (captive-finance P/E). Its ABS debt (EUR 8.4bn) funds its own receivables and is excluded from net debt; its flows are excluded from the automotive build. FY2025 AR results of operations.

equity_bridge.item: Equity-accounted and held-for-sale investments (incl. Bugatti Rimac / Rimac stakes) at book
equity_bridge.note: Equity-accounted investments EUR 703m at 31-Dec-2025; EUR 411m reclassified held-for-sale at 30-Jun-2026 for the Rimac/Bugatti exit (overlapping); share of profit sits in the financial result, which the EBITDA build excludes, so the asset is added here (matching-asset rule).

equity_bridge.item: Pension provisions, net of 30% tax shield
equity_bridge.note: Provisions for pensions EUR 3,530m at 31-Dec-2025 (discount rate 4.3%); debt-like, service cost already in EBITDA. Not in automotive net liquidity.

historical_growth.owner_fcf_series_note: Automotive net cash flow less interest income (EUR m): 3,676-425, 3,866-461, 3,973-264, 3,735-278, 1,511-188. SBC is zero, so owner and reported CAGRs differ only by the interest strip. Only FY2021-FY2025 exist (IPO Sept-2022), so the longest CAGR is 4 years; 5-year fields are null, not zero.
historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_4yr_cagr (FY2021-25), cross-checked against the CMD mid-term ambition of EUR 41-45bn group revenue (+14-25% vs FY2025). Equity CAGR not used: FY2022 equity fell from 22.9bn to 17.0bn on the pre-IPO capital restructuring / special distribution to VW, so the 3-year equity CAGR (10.5%) measures a rebound from an artificial low, and the 4-year (0.1%) measures nothing.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (3yr 10.5%) diverges >30% from revenue (-1.2%) and EPS (-55.8%) CAGRs. All three are distorted: equity by the 2022 pre-IPO restructuring, EPS and FCF by the FY2024-25 trough (EUR 3.1bn realignment charges, tariffs, China). None is a usable forward growth rate; forward path is anchored to FY2026 guidance and the Oct-2026 CMD mid-term ambition instead.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF 3yr CAGR (-27.0%) is the trough talking: FY2021-24 owner FCF was a stable EUR 3.25-3.7bn (10-12% of automotive revenue). The model normalises toward ~EUR 3.2bn by FY2030 in the base case -- roughly back to the pre-trough level in euros on a larger revenue base, i.e. a lower margin than FY2021-23.

scenario_narratives.base: Porsche delivers roughly the lower bracket of its own October-2026 mid-term ambition, a little late. FY2026 is the trough year management guided (automotive EBITDA ~16%, NCF margin 3-5%) with a product gap from the 718 run-out and the end of ICE Macan production. From 2027 the refreshed line-up -- electric Cayenne, the combustion/hybrid Macan successor that the 2025 strategy reversal brought back, 911 derivatives -- plus the cost programme lift automotive revenue to ~EUR 38bn and EBITDA margins to ~21.5% by 2030. That is a good business again (auto RoS ~13%, owner-FCF ~EUR 3.2bn) but not the 18-19% RoS Porsche of 2021-23: US tariffs, a smaller and cheaper China, a strong euro and elevated D&A from the EV write-down cycle are treated as permanent.
scenario_narratives.bull: The brand proves intact and pricing power returns: 'value over volume' plus the new SUVs and a strong 911 cycle push automotive revenue past EUR 41bn by 2030 and EBITDA margins back to ~24% (auto RoS ~15.5%, the CMD strategic ambition of 15%). US tariffs are partly absorbed by pricing and local-content deals, China stabilises at ~40-45k units at better mix, the battery/BEV write-downs leave capex discipline behind them, and owner FCF margin returns to ~10%, inside management's 9-12% NCF ambition.
scenario_narratives.bear: The 2024-26 damage is structural. China keeps shrinking as local EV makers take the premium segment, US tariffs stay and widen, the BEV share stalls while CO2 regulation forces compliance cost, and the product push lands into a soft luxury market with VW-group platform delays. Automotive revenue barely recovers (~EUR 34bn by 2030), EBITDA margins plateau at ~18% with D&A stuck near 9% (auto RoS ~9%), and owner FCF settles around EUR 2bn -- a premium automaker earning an ordinary automaker's return, closer to BMW/Mercedes economics than to Ferrari's.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the car company on a normalised, mid-cycle owner-FCF path rather than on the FY2025 trough or the FY2021-23 peak. The trough (auto RoS 0.3%, owner FCF EUR 1.3bn) is dominated by EUR 3.1bn of one-off realignment charges and would undervalue the franchise by more than half if extrapolated; the peak (RoS 18.6%) predates US tariffs and the China reset and would overvalue it. The base path converges on the lower end of management's own mid-term ambition, the captive finance arm is valued separately so its ABS funding does not masquerade as enterprise debt, and pensions are charged as debt.
key_risks_to_valuation: Margin recovery is the whole thesis: each 1pp of mature automotive EBITDA margin is worth roughly EUR 2.5-3 per share.
China: deliveries fell from ~95k (2021) to ~42k (2025) and local premium EVs keep taking share; the base case assumes stabilisation, not recovery.
US tariffs (15% since Jul-2025) with no US production; any increase hits margin directly.
Product execution after the 2025 strategy reversal (BEV launches postponed, combustion/hybrid derivatives reinstated, new EV platform rescheduled) -- further write-downs possible.

Governance: Volkswagen AG and Porsche SE control the ordinary shares; P911 preferred holders have no vote, and capital allocation (dividends, intra-group pricing, VW platform costs) is set by the controlling shareholder.
Q3 2026 results on 27-Oct-2026 may move FY2026 anchors; refresh after the print.
sanity_check P/E trip is a trough-denominator artefact (FY2025 EPS); it should clear once FY2026 (guided auto RoS recovery) becomes latest FY -- if it does not, revisit the margin path.
valuation_philosophy.trough_pe_distortion: sanity_check trips on implied P/E (~99x) only because its denominator is FY2025 net income less SBC -- a trough year carrying EUR 3.1bn of realignment, BEV-Macan and impairment charges (automotive RoS 0.3%). The market price itself is ~88x on the same denominator, and P/B (1.85x vs 10y 1.6-5.8x), EV/EBITDA (8.4x vs 6.3-10.5x) and P/Sales (1.17x vs 1.0-2.6x) all sit inside their historical ranges. Clearing the 2x-average P/E rule (68x) would need a weighted IV of ~EUR 32, below the bear case and 23% under the market price; no defensible WACC clears it (base at 12% is EUR 37.0, because the 12x FCF terminal cap binds at every rate at or below 9%). Decision (2026-10-25): no driver change. WACC stays 9.0% = CoE (Bund 2.7% + beta 1.15 x ERP 5.5%): cyclicality is already in the beta, China/tariff risk is priced in the scenario flows and the 25% bear weight, and the 'customer concentration' diagnosis does not apply to a retail luxury-auto OEM selling ~280k cars a year to individuals. Treat the P/E trip as a known false positive; re-test after FY2026 earnings replace the trough denominator.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API for P911.DE at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 35.62-50.66 EUR.
data_sources.financials: Porsche AG Annual and Sustainability Report FY2025 (automotive net cash flow table, third-party borrowings note, pensions, segment results); Half-Year Financial Report H1 2026 (automotive net liquidity bridge at 30-Jun-2026, automotive NCF); H1 2026 analyst presentation (FY2026 outlook, reconfirmed); Capital Markets Day presentation 7-Oct-2026 (mid-term ambition: revenue EUR 41-45bn, RoS 10-15%, auto NCF margin 9-12%, lower bracket expected); Q3 2026 pre-close call 13-Oct-2026 (YTD deliveries); P911.DE_Metrics.csv / kpis table for FY2021-25 history.
data_sources.qualitative: No Analysis JSON at build time; scenario axes drawn from the filings above (product gap, strategy realignment, China, tariffs, cost programme) and the CMD framework.

inputs.share_count_basis: 911.0m shares = 455.5m ordinary + 455.5m preferred (FY2025 AR 'Total number of shares' 911,000,000; basic = diluted, no dilutive instruments). Preferred shares (the listed P911 line) carry a EUR 0.01 dividend preference and are otherwise treated as economically equivalent to the ordinary shares held by Porsche SE/VW. Held flat: no buybacks, no equity-settled SBC, no non-SBC issuance expected.
inputs.sbc_source: No equity-settled share-based payment: Porsche AG executive LTI (performance share plan) is cash-settled and already expensed in personnel cost / operating cash flow; EquityAwardTaxes 0 every year. SBC-zero market treatment (owner-fcf-adaptations (e)).
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-23T15:36:58Z (Yahoo chart API, P911.DE regular session, last trade before the weekend; Q3 2026 report due 2026-10-27 -- refresh after it)
inputs.wacc_rationale: EUR flows, EUR rate. German 10y Bund ~2.7% + beta ~1.15 (cyclical premium-auto, VW-controlled, free float ~25% of prefs) x ERP 5.5% = cost of equity ~9.0%. Automotive segment is net cash (EUR 7.3bn net liquidity), so WACC = CoE = 9.0%, identical across scenarios: cyclicality, China and tariff risk are priced in the scenario flows and the 25% bear weight, not stacked on the rate (owner-fcf-adaptations (f)).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt: automotive third-party borrowings (EUR 2,260m at 30-Jun-2026) include the IFRS 16 lease liabilities (~EUR 1.15bn group; FY2025 note 'Total third-party borrowings' table: ABS 8,353 / debt securities 781 / other 1,133 / leases 1,164, of which only the non-ABS automotive part sits in the automotive figure), so lease principal is NOT deducted from flows and EBITDA is post-IFRS 16. Lease renewal (~EUR 135m/yr principal, ~0.4% of revenue) is absorbed in the capex path, which is held ~0.5pp above D&A at maturity.
inputs.nci_treatment: Immaterial: NCI equity EUR -121m (25% of Porsche Singapore, 49% minority stakes); NCI share of profit < EUR 10m most years. Flows treated as attributable; no bridge deduction.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF (component route) on the AUTOMOTIVE segment, plus a sum-of-parts bridge. Routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 'Operating company, non-US or cyclical' + owner-fcf-adaptations. Why segment, not group: the group cash flow statement and the group 'total debt' of EUR 11.4bn are dominated by Porsche Financial Services (ABS refinancing EUR 8.4bn funding lease/loan receivables). A captive finance arm's debt is operating funding, not enterprise net debt (same principle as bank deposits), and its receivable growth makes group FCF (EUR 478m FY2025) meaningless for the car business. So: (1) flows = automotive segment, base revenue = automotive sales revenue FY2025 ~EUR 32,170m (derived from automotive EBITDA 4,282 / 13.3% margin and automotive NCF 1,511 / 4.7%; group revenue 36,272 incl. FS 4,384 less consolidation); (2) net cash = automotive net liquidity EUR 7,302m at 30-Jun-2026 (gross liquidity 9,562 less automotive third-party borrowings 2,260, H1 2026 report p.14); (3) Financial Services, equity-accounted stakes and pensions enter via equity_bridge. Owner FCF FY0 = automotive net cash flow 1,511 - interest income 188 = 1,323 (the component build uses EBITDA and so excludes the financial result entirely; net liquidity is in the bridge). NORMALISATION: FY2025 is a trough, not a base -- automotive EBITDA margin 13.3% vs 24.5-25.7% in FY2021-23; auto RoS 0.3% after ~EUR 3.1bn of product-strategy realignment charges (BEV launch postponements, new-platform rescheduling, Cellforce battery exit), 15% US tariffs and China deliveries down to ~42k. The FY2025 margin is NOT carried forward. Year 1 (FY2026) is anchored to confirmed guidance (group revenue EUR 35-36bn, group RoS 5.5-7.5%, automotive EBITDA margin 15-17%, automotive NCF margin 3-5%; reconfirmed H1 2026; H1 actual auto EBITDA margin 18.3%, NCF margin 6.7%). The recovery path is anchored to the 7-Oct-2026 Capital Markets Day mid-term ambition (group revenue EUR 41-45bn, group RoS 10-15%, automotive NCF margin 9-12%), which management itself says will 'more likely settle within the lower bracket'. Base case lands at roughly the lower end of that ambition (mature auto EBITDA 21.5%, D&A 8.5%, RoS ~13%, owner-FCF margin ~8.3% ex interest income, i.e. ~8.8% on management's NCF definition) -- deliberately well below the FY2021-23 run rate (NCF margin 10.6-12.1%, RoS 18.6%), because tariffs, China and elevated D&A from the EV write-down cycle look structural rather than transitory. Horizon 10 years because margins are still recovering through year 5. Terminal capped at 12x FCF (cyclical). Price is the preferred share; ordinary shares are unlisted and assumed equal value per share. The planned sale of the Bugatti Rimac / Rimac Group stakes (EUR 411m held for sale at 30-Jun-2026) is included at book in the bridge.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 automotive revenue -2% (group guide EUR 35-36bn vs 36.3bn; product gap from 718 end-of-production and ICE Macan run-out, YTD Q3 deliveries 178.5k vs 212.5k). Recovery 2027-30 on the product push (ICE/hybrid Macan successor, electric Cayenne ramp from summer 2026, 911/derivative mix, 'value over volume' pricing) to automotive revenue ~EUR 38bn by FY2030, i.e. the lower end of the CMD EUR 41-45bn group ambition. Then GDP-plus luxury growth fading to 2.5%.
base.margin_rationale: Automotive EBITDA margin 16% in FY2026 (guide 15-17%; H1 actual 18.3% includes provision reversals), recovering to 21.5% -- four points below FY2021-23 (24.5-25.7%) because of 15% US tariffs, lower China volume at lower price points, stronger EUR and the regulatory cost base, all of which management itself treats as persistent in its CMD framework. Cost programme ('Zukunftspaket', headcount cuts) offsets part of it.
base.da_rationale: D&A 9.7% FY2026 falling to 8.5%: management explicitly guides 'persistently elevated D&A' after capitalised BEV development and the platform rescheduling; FY2021-23 auto D&A ran ~7%. FY2025's ~13% included impairments and is not repeatable.
base.capex_rationale: Capex here = automotive PP&E/intangible capex + capitalised development + equity investments (the investing line of automotive NCF). FY2025 10.4%, H1 2026 9.4%, FY2021-23 ~10-11% incl. capitalised R&D. Mature 9.0%, held 0.5pp above D&A to fund lease renewals and growth.
base.tax_rationale: German group statutory ~30% (effective tax rate 30.4% FY2025, 31.2% FY2024). FY2025 cash tax of EUR 317m on PBT 445m was refund/timing-distorted; not carried.
base.wc_rationale: Manufacturer: inventories ~EUR 6.0bn + receivables less payables ~14% of automotive revenue, so growth consumes cash at ~14% of the revenue increment.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: the recovery rests on an unproven product push after a reversed EV strategy, with China, tariffs and CO2 rules outside management's control, and the CMD ambition itself is flagged by management as likely lower-bracket. Base 50% because FY2026 guidance has been reconfirmed and H1 2026 is tracking at or above it (auto EBITDA 18.3%, NCF 6.7%). Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things -- tariff relief, China stabilisation, full pricing recovery -- to go right together. Balance sheet risk is nil (EUR 7.3bn automotive net cash), so no solvency tail is priced.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)

diagnosis.detail: Structural risks in the qualitative analysis that a standard WACC may not price: customer concentration, cyclicality
Projected growth 2.3% exceeds the through-cycle revenue CAGR 2.3%

fix_applied.change: none -- driver paths and WACC (9.0%) left unchanged; trip judged a false positive
fix_applied.reason: Implied P/E is measured against FY2025 trough net income (EUR 3.1bn realignment/impairment charges, auto RoS 0.3%). The market price itself is ~88x on that denominator. Passing the 2x-average rule (68.4x) needs weighted IV <= ~EUR 31.9 (below the bear case, 23% under price); base IV at 12% WACC is still EUR 37.0 because the 12x terminal cap binds. P/B, EV/EBITDA and P/Sales all pass. Cyclicality is already in beta 1.15; China/tariff risk is in the flows and 25% bear weight; customer concentration does not apply.
